newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hails U.S. on Cuba law but wants it scrapped.
newsitem.headline: France hails U.S. on Cuba law but wants it scrapped.

text.p: France on Saturday applauded U.S. President Bill Clinton's suspension of a law imposing sanctions on Communist-ruled Cuba but again urged him to drop it entirely.
The foreign ministry welcomed Clinton's suspension for another six months of the Helms-Burton law section providing for judicial action against any company doing business with Cuba.

But the ministry added in a statement: "France remains concerned that section IV of the Helms-Burton law allowing American authorities to ban access to U.S. territory for company managers targeted by this law remains in force.
"France can only reiterate its opposition to such unilateral measures and calls for the respect of rules guaranteeing security and freedom of international trade," it said.
France appealed to Clinton to "use the powers at his disposal, as he has just shown, to avoid (the law's) application".
France has been one of the loudest opponents of the Helms-Burton act that would allow Americans to sue foreigners with certain investments in Cuba.

On Friday, Clinton said he would continue a six-month suspension of the bill for a further half year, after receiving assurances from its opponents, including Canada and the European Commission, that they were working to help bring democracy to Cuba.
